summary: This lecture from Shaykh Ali Mashhour's Zadul-Ma'ad series covers the Prophet Muhammad's journey to Ta'if to seek protection and spread Islam after losing his protectors Abu Talib and his wife Khadijah. The people of Ta'if rejected him and caused him physical harm, after which he retreated to an orchard in despair. Despite this hardship, a group of jinn heard his Quranic recitation and accepted Islam. The Prophet was eventually able to return to Mecca under the protection of Mut'im ibn Adi. The lecture then discusses Al-Isra and Al-Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension), explaining that this miraculous event occurred physically with both body and soul, not merely as a spiritual vision, and clarifying misconceptions about depictions of Al-Buraq in Islamic art.
